title: Relative assassin points persist as generic points on nearby fibres
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a locally finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite type [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $\xi\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X/S}(F)$ [def-trf-relative-assassin]. Give $Z=\overline{\{\xi\}}\subseteq X$ its reduced induced closed subscheme structure [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. There exists a nonempty open subscheme $W\subseteq Z$ [def-weil-open-immersion] such that, for every $s\in f(W)$, the image in $X_s$ of every generic point of every irreducible component of $W_s$ belongs to $\operatorname{Ass}_{X_s}(F_s)$ [def-sc-generic-point, def-weil-irreducible-components]. Here $W_s$ and $X_s$ are scheme-theoretic fibres [def-pc-scheme-fibre], $F_s$ is tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], and $W_s\to X_s$ is induced by $W\to Z\to X$. No flatness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Choose an affine neighbourhood of $f(\xi)$ and an affine neighbourhood $U$ of $\xi$ over it on which $F$ is represented by $\widetilde M$. We may work on these neighbourhoods: $Z\cap U$ is open in $Z$, and associatedness is defined on stalks, which are unchanged on an open. Write the charts as $\operatorname{Spec}A$, $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$. The affine-pair criterion gives $B$ finite type over $A$, and the finite-type affine module criterion gives $M$ finite over $B$. Write $\mathfrak q$ for $\xi$ and $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap A$. The affine fibre comparison identifies $U_s$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A\kappa(s))$, and tensor pullback identifies $F_s|_{U_s}$ with the module sheaf of $M\otimes_A\kappa(s)$. These fibre rings are finite type over fields (the images of a finite set of algebra generators still generate), hence Noetherian. By the relative-assassin definition and the affine associated-point comparison, the fibre prime of $\xi$ is associated to $M\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.

source.place: Tag 05F1 (lemma-relative-assassin-in-neighbourhood), first paragraph, affine charts and the associated generic-fibre prime

proof.text: Replace the rings and module by $A_0=A/\mathfrak p$, $B_0=B/\mathfrak pB$, $M_0=M/\mathfrak pM$, and $\mathfrak q_0=\mathfrak q/\mathfrak pB$. The domain $A_0$ injects into $B_0/\mathfrak q_0=B/\mathfrak q$; its fraction field is $K=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. The fibre module at the generic point of $\operatorname{Spec}A_0$ is the original $M\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Associated-prime transport from the fibre ring says precisely that $\mathfrak q_0$ is the annihilator of an element of $M_0\otimes_{A_0}K$ considered as a $B_0$-module. These replacements do not alter $Z\cap U=\operatorname{Spec}(B/\mathfrak q)$. For a prime $\mathfrak r\supseteq\mathfrak p$, the residue fields of $A$ at $\mathfrak r$ and of $A_0$ at $\mathfrak r/\mathfrak p$ agree, and $(M/\mathfrak pM)\otimes_{A/\mathfrak p}\kappa(\mathfrak r)=M\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak r)$, since every element of $\mathfrak p$ acts as zero on that field. The identical ring formula gives the same ambient fibres. Thus it suffices to prove the conclusion for $(A_0,B_0,M_0,\mathfrak q_0)$; rename them $(A,B,M,\mathfrak q)$, with $A$ a domain and $\mathfrak q\cap A=0$.

source.place: Tag 05F1 (lemma-relative-assassin-in-neighbourhood), first paragraph, quotient by the image prime and preservation of fibres

proof.text: Apply simultaneous generic flatness to the domain $A$, the finite-type $A$-algebra $B$, and the finite $B$-module $M$. Choose $0\ne a\in A$ so that $M_a$ is flat as an $A$-module. Set $B'=B[1/a]$, $M'=M[1/a]$, and $\mathfrak q'=\mathfrak qB'$. Here $B'$ remains finite type over $A$ (adjoin $a^{-1}$), $M'$ remains finite over $B'$, and $\mathfrak q'$ is prime with contraction zero to $A$. Since $a$ is already invertible in $K$, the generic-fibre module and its associated point have not changed.

source.place: Tag 05F1 (lemma-relative-assassin-in-neighbourhood), second paragraph, first generic-flatness application

proof.text: Choose $z\in M'\otimes_AK$ whose annihilator as a $B'$-module is $\mathfrak q'$; the same fibre-associated-prime transport applies after localization. Write $z=m/c$ with $m\in M'$ and $0\ne c\in A$. Multiplication by $c$ is invertible on this localization, so $m/1$ has the same annihilator as $z$. Flatness over the domain makes $M'$ torsion-free. The localization map $M'\to M'\otimes_AK$ is injective: an element in its kernel is killed by some nonzero element of $A$, hence is zero. Consequently $bm=0$ if and only if $b(m/1)=0$, and $\operatorname{Ann}_{B'}(m)=\mathfrak q'$. The explicit map $B'/\mathfrak q'\to M'$, $\bar b\mapsto bm$, is therefore well-defined and injective. Let $Q$ be its cokernel. The images of any finite generating set of $M'$ generate $Q$, so $Q$ is finite over $B'$.

source.place: Tag 05F1 (lemma-relative-assassin-in-neighbourhood), third paragraph, the annihilator proof of the associated-prime lift and the cyclic injection

proof.text: Apply simultaneous generic flatness again, now to $A\to B'$ and its finite module $Q$. Obtain $0\ne b\in A$ with $Q_b$ flat as an $A$-module. Set $B''=B'[1/b]$, $M''=M'[1/b]$, and $C=(B'/\mathfrak q')[1/b]=(B/\mathfrak q)[1/(ab)]$. Localizing the preceding short exact sequence gives $0\to C\to M''\to Q_b\to0$. Explicitly, a fraction in the kernel is killed by a power of $b$ in the original cokernel, so that multiplying its numerator by that power puts it in the original image; injectivity follows by the same fraction-zero criterion. Thus no finite-presentation hypothesis on $Q$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 05F1 (lemma-relative-assassin-in-neighbourhood), third paragraph, second generic-flatness application and localization of the sequence

proof.text: For every prime $\mathfrak r$ of $A$, flatness of the cokernel $Q_b$ and the flat-quotient tensor-injectivity theorem give an injection $C\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak r)\hookrightarrow M''\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak r)$. Put $W=\operatorname{Spec}C$, viewed as the principal open $D(ab)$ in $\operatorname{Spec}(B/\mathfrak q)=Z\cap U$. The affine fibre and pullback comparisons identify $W_s$ with $\operatorname{Spec}D_s$, where $D_s=C\otimes_A\kappa(s)$, and the ambient open fibre with $\operatorname{Spec}R_s$, where $R_s=B''\otimes_A\kappa(s)$. The displayed injection is $R_s$-linear. Moreover $D_s=R_s/(\mathfrak q B''\cdot R_s)$: tensoring the quotient is the quotient by the images of its relations, as is checked by $\bar x\otimes\lambda\leftrightarrow(x\otimes\lambda)\bmod\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Tag 05F1 (lemma-relative-assassin-in-neighbourhood), third paragraph, universal injectivity and its fibre interpretation

proof.text: Fix $s\in f(W)$ and any generic point $y$ of an irreducible component of $W_s=\operatorname{Spec}D_s$. Its prime $P\subset D_s$ is minimal. Both $R_s$ and its quotient $D_s$ are finite type over the field $\kappa(s)$, hence Noetherian. The minimal-prime-associated theorem supplies $d\in D_s$ with $\operatorname{Ann}_{D_s}(d)=P$. Let $j:D_s\hookrightarrow M''\otimes_A\kappa(s)$ be the injection above. For $r\in R_s$, $rj(d)=0$ if and only if $\bar r d=0$, since $j$ is injective. Hence the annihilator of $j(d)$ over $R_s$ is the inverse image of $P$, exactly the prime of the image of $y$ in the ambient fibre. The affine associated-point comparison implies that this image belongs to $\operatorname{Ass}_{X_s}(F_s)$; associatedness on the ambient affine open is the same stalk condition as in $X_s$.

source.place: Tag 05F1 (lemma-relative-assassin-in-neighbourhood), final sentences, minimal fibre primes are associated and injection preserves their annihilators

proof.text: Finally, the elements $a,b\in A\setminus\{0\}$ have nonzero images in the domain $B/\mathfrak q$, because $\mathfrak q\cap A=0$. Thus $W=D(ab)\subseteq Z\cap U$ contains its generic point $\xi$ and is nonempty. It is open in the original $Z$. The quotient-base identifications in Step 2 and the unchanged stalks on the chosen opens carry Step 7 back to the original $X,S,F$. This proves every asserted fibre-generic-point clause, without assuming the original base or source Noetherian or $F$ flat.

source.place: Tag 05F1 (lemma-relative-assassin-in-neighbourhood), completion of the affine reduction and nonemptiness of the chosen open
